drhp.business: The Company manufactures copper cables and wires, with its primary focus on copper conductors used in transformers. Its product portfolio includes bare copper strips and wires, paper covered copper strips and wires (Kraft/Crepe/Nomex/Mica), copper tapes, fibre glass covered copper strips and wires, copper rods and flats, submersible wires and bunched conductors, sold principally to transformer manufacturing companies in India.
drhp.expansion: The Company operates two manufacturing units, at Odhav, Ahmedabad and at Bavla, Ahmedabad. Additional manufacturing capacity was commissioned and ramped up during the year under review at these units, contributing to the growth in gross block and depreciation during FY26.

risks.note: A sharp movement in the London Metal Exchange price of copper, or in the exchange rate, can affect realisation, inventory valuation and working capital requirement.
Economic downturns and disruptions can affect demand for construction and infrastructure projects, and consequently the Company's sales.
Global supply chain disruptions can affect the production and delivery of raw materials.
The business-to-business copper conductor, cable and wire industry is highly competitive, with established players and new entrants including large integrated manufacturers.
Operations are funded in part by working capital and term borrowings, and an increase in interest rates would increase finance cost.
Reliance on a limited set of suppliers for copper cathode and rod may expose the Company to supply chain vulnerabilities.
Significant reliance on the transformer segment makes the Company susceptible to the investment cycle in that industry.
Growth in inventories and receivables from scaling up operations, together with elevated copper prices, increases working capital requirement and associated finance cost.

Its product portfolio includes bare copper strips and wires, paper covered copper strips and wires (Kraft/Crepe/Nomex/Mica), copper tapes, fibre glass covered copper strips and wires, copper rods and flats, submersible wires and bunched conductors, sold principally to transformer manufacturing companies in India.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained transmission and distribution capital expenditure (National Electricity Plan, Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme) driving demand for power and distribution transformers and hence for paper covered and bare copper conductors.
- Renewable energy and rooftop solar build-out (500 GW non-fossil target by 2030, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana) generating demand for transformers, inverter duty transformers, solar cables and associated conductors.
- Data centre and digital infrastructure build-out creating price-inelastic demand for high-quality power distribution equipment.
- Electrification of transport, railways and metro projects adding to conductor and cable consumption.
- Government-led housing, smart cities and industrial-corridor investment, aided by production linked incentive schemes, generating demand for housing wires, low-voltage cables and industrial cabling.
- Commissioning and ramp-up of new domestic copper smelting/refining capacity expected to improve availability of refined copper in India and reduce dependence on imported cathode, benefiting downstream manufacturers such as the Company.
- The transformer manufacturing industry (the Company's principal end-market) has recorded strong order inflows and is expanding capacity, and the Company is favourably positioned as a supplier of copper conductors to participate in this cycle.
- Copper, the Company's single largest input, remained firm/elevated due to constrained mine supply and concentrate tightness, placing a premium on procurement discipline and the ability to pass through input cost movements to customers.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates two manufacturing units, at Odhav, Ahmedabad and at Bavla, Ahmedabad. Additional manufacturing capacity was commissioned and ramped up during the year under review at these units, contributing to the growth in gross block and depreciation during FY26.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- A sharp movement in the London Metal Exchange price of copper, or in the exchange rate, can affect realisation, inventory valuation and working capital requirement.
- Economic downturns and disruptions can affect demand for construction and infrastructure projects, and consequently the Company's sales.
- Global supply chain disruptions can affect the production and delivery of raw materials.
- The business-to-business copper conductor, cable and wire industry is highly competitive, with established players and new entrants including large integrated manufacturers.
- Operations are funded in part by working capital and term borrowings, and an increase in interest rates would increase finance cost.
- Reliance on a limited set of suppliers for copper cathode and rod may expose the Company to supply chain vulnerabilities.
- Significant reliance on the transformer segment makes the Company susceptible to the investment cycle in that industry.
- Growth in inventories and receivables from scaling up operations, together with elevated copper prices, increases working capital requirement and associated finance cost.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to invest in plant and machinery to support scaling up of operations.
- Broaden the product mix towards higher value-added paper covered and fibre glass covered conductors.
- Deepen relationships with transformer manufacturers.
- Strengthen receivables management and cash conversion.
- Institutionalise the governance and compliance framework as a listed entity.
